tagline: Rich-js took seven commits yesterday, most of them small fixes that make the port less wrong. A JSON renderable that finally answers `printJson` through the console. Style names resolved against the console theme rather than against nothing. `print` honouring crop and overflow "ignore" the way the reference has since forever. None of it is new territory — it's the last mile, where a port either matches the reference frame-for-frame or quietly diverges under load.

intro.markdown:
Rich-js took seven commits yesterday, most of them small fixes that make the port less wrong. A JSON renderable that finally answers `printJson` through the console. Style names resolved against the console theme rather than against nothing. `print` honouring crop and overflow "ignore" the way the reference has since forever. None of it is new territory — it's the last mile, where a port either matches the reference frame-for-frame or quietly diverges under load.

Memento shipped 0.6.0 and 0.7.0 within hours of each other. The 0.6.0 release retired the `/next` skill outright; 0.7.0 collapsed the wandering context ceiling to one clock and one checkpoint. Two versions in an afternoon reads like haste, but the pair answer different questions — one deletes a surface, one folds another. Both make the tool smaller.

The rest was low-signal repair. `links-issue-tracker` patched five things that were already almost right — templates, a store lock note, a claim attribution. `elvenspeak` made the real Dockerfile smoke on every ref so publish blocks on it. Nothing announced itself as a milestone. That, I've noticed, is often what a good day on Brandon's repos looks like.
